summary.headline: Century Enka Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 554 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.46%, helped by a Rs 46.24 crore one-time inventory gain.
summary.overview: Revenue of Rs 554 crore grew 38% YoY and 15% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 86 crore (up 331% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 62 crore (up 301% YoY). Management attributed the margin jump partly to a one-time inventory gain from low-cost opening stock (Rs 46.24 crore as reported) and partly to GST-cut-driven auto and tyre demand, pass-through pricing and a higher renewable power share above 40%. Management said margins are expected to normalise, and it kept its normalised operating margin range at 7-10%.

financial_highlights.change: Per management, as reported in the results filing

segments.name: Tyre cord fabric (NTCF/PTCF)
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 306 crore, up 69% YoY. Demand is described as robust after GST cuts on tyres and autos. PTCF approvals are progressing, with commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.

segments.name: Filament yarn
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 230 crore, up 20% YoY, with healthy demand and better mix from valuated and mother yarn products. Cheap Chinese commodity imports persist, and anti-dumping duty was not notified despite favourable DGTR findings.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to normalise over the next few quarters as higher-cost inventory is consumed. Normalised operating margin range maintained at 7-10%; management said it would revise this only once it is confident the range has moved up.
Renewable power share is over 40% in Q1; expected to reach about 50% once the Bharuch group captive expansion (about 10-10.5 MW capacity) commissions, most likely in Q3 FY27 or H2.
PTCF commercial sales expected to start in H2 FY27, possibly Q3 or Q4.
No significant capacity addition in FY27. Mother yarn capacity addition to commission in FY28, adding about 3-4 thousand tonnes per annum.
Capex of over Rs 100 crore planned for FY27, covering value-added yarn products, power-cost reduction and safety upgrades.
No forward guidance on realisations, volumes or the quantum of margin impact from raw material costs.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 92,000 MTPA; utilisation normally runs at 85-90%, varying by product.
Capex of over Rs 100 crore in FY27, including value-added filament yarn products (adds to margins, not capacity) and power-cost reduction.
Bharuch group captive renewable scheme adds about 10-10.5 MW; Century Enka's equity contribution is about 26%, with about Rs 8.5 crore spent so far.
Mother yarn capacity addition to commission in FY28; PTCF plant is under approval, and the company is selling some yarn in the meantime, which affects capacity.
Management said new investments must clear board-approved hurdle rates, typically a minimum 12-15% IRR.
demand_pricing: Tyre-cord demand is robust after the September 2025 GST cuts on tyres and autos; management could not quantify the GST contribution to the 38% growth, but said Q3 onwards showed a stark improvement.
Management flagged geopolitical events, volatile crude, inflation and cheap imports as risks to domestic demand. Exports are very small.
Caprolactam and chips prices spiked after the Iran war and have since eased but remain volatile. A sharp move within one to two months affects gross margin.
Realisations are not guided because pricing changes month to month.

Raw material inventory is about 25-30 days for imports (including in transit) and about 10-15 days (around 15) for domestic sourcing. Management does not see raw material availability as a constraint.
Volumes have been broadly flat over the past four years per an analyst; management said FY27 volume depends on market conditions and import competition.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the inventory gain add to the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the Rs 46.24 crore inventory impact already in the results filing and declined to say whether it applies at EBITDA level or to give any further breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renewable power share and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power was over 40% of consumption in Q1. It is expected to rise to about 50% after the Bharuch expansion commissions, and management did not quantify the value impact.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 38% growth came from GST-cut-led demand, and is there a risk of air-pocketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify the GST effect. It said auto sales across segments kept growing quarter-on-quarter, and that how long the effect lasts depends on financing and the economy.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin stayed at 58-59% for three quarters, and what is the normalised EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked gross margin to volume growth and to inventory timing on sharp raw material moves. It reiterated a normalised operating margin of 7-10% and said anything above that may not be permanent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin range move to 10% or double digits on a sustainable basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide. It said the range would be revised only once it is confident the improvement is durable, and it would not be breached at least in normal circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex, and what is the capacity outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is over Rs 100 crore in FY27. Capacity is not expected to rise in FY27, with about 3-4 thousand tonnes per annum added in FY28 from mother yarn.

risks_watch: Reversal of the one-time inventory gain and normalisation of margins as higher-cost caprolactam and chips inventory is consumed. Management did not quantify either.
Demand softening after the GST-driven tyre and auto boost, plus crude, geopolitical and inflation risks.
Cheap Chinese filament yarn imports, with anti-dumping duty still not notified.
PTCF commercial sales timing (H2 FY27) and whether the approvals hold.
Renewable power share rising to about 50% and the Bharuch commissioning timing (Q3 FY27 expected).
Volume growth has been flat over four years per an analyst, and FY27 capacity is not expanding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's headline numbers, but guarded on forward margins, realisations and volumes, which management repeatedly declined to guide. It stressed that the 7-10% normalised range is unchanged while also saying margins will normalise, and it was evasive on the inventory gain quantum and the GST demand split.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report an exceptional quarter with the company delivering record revenue growth, profitability growth and margin performance.
Inventory impact is Rs. 46.24 crores, which is already mentioned in our quarterly results submission to the stock exchanges.
We do expect to spend over 100 crores in CAPEX in the current year, current financial year.
So, we are not adding any significant volumes in the current financial year in terms of capacity addition.
Normally, we are looking forward for 12 % to 15% minimum IR when we initiate the project.
